2016_090_021616mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of February 16, 2016 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, pairing athletic and student recognitions and January minutes with the December 2015 Treasurer's Report and four business items. Total disbursements in the period were $10,185,127.18, of which $8,084,034.91 was check disbursements. The Board was asked to rescind its resolution for a written agreement with the Beijing Weiming Education Group after Oakland Schools declined to extend its SEVIS certification to the arrangement, and to award roofing, lawn-mowing and bond-construction bids and engage Lusk Albertson as policy services provider.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, February 16, 2016, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session; video at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
Senior Scholar Athletes 2015-2016, honoring athletes with a 3.5 cumulative grade point average at Troy High, Athens and the International Academy. Fall 2015 All-State Athletes: Noah Arabbo (Athens, boys soccer), Jennifer Cui and Naomi Kim (girls golf), Michael Faber, Kevin Fietsam, Steve Forman and Sai Kagithala (boys tennis), and Bogdan Pintilie (boys soccer), all Troy High. A resolution recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. A Mission Moment honors Barnard fourth graders in the Oakland County Water Resources Commission Kids' Clean Water Calendar Contest, which drew over 800 county entries and produced four Barnard grand winners.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the January 12, 2016 workshop and of the January 19, 2016 organizational and regular meeting, where motions 16-001 through 16-015 all carried 7-0: Dr. Philippart president, Mr. Schmidt vice president, Mrs. Fleming secretary and Rick L. West treasurer, each through December 31, 2016; depositories and legal counsel designated; Mr. Pass appointed Director of Employee Services. Also the December 2015 Treasurer's Report and rescission of the Weiming resolution.

**General Fund budget report, December year-to-date FY2016**
Revenue budget $139,930,708 against actual $48,501,769, leaving $91,428,939 or 65.34% uncollected. Expenditure budget $141,360,708 against actual $56,294,256 with $50,129,908 encumbered and $34,936,543 (24.71%) available. Excess revenue over (under) expenditures (1,430,000). Fund balance $20,701,637 at December 1, 2015 and $19,271,637 at December 31, 2015.

**Other fund balances at December 31, 2015**

Consolidated special revenue $4,552,646; food service (520) $1,469,339; Troy Career Center (529) $0; adult and community education (530) $2,641,522; facilities rental (535) $441,785; consolidated debt service $970,056; consolidated capital projects (499, 414) $669,273.

**Weiming / SEVIS**
Superintendent Rich Machesky's January 22, 2016 email to the Board reports that Oakland Schools will not extend its SEVIS certification for F1 visas to a Troy partnership with Weiming, so Troy will not enter the MOU; obtaining its own certification would take more than 9 months. Districts hosting Educatius students receive the per pupil allocation plus an additional $2000.

**Enrollment projections (report, no action)**
Prepared February 2, 2016 by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., STANFRED Consultants. Headcount rose from 12,182 in 2007/08 to 12,710 in 2015/16; Schools of Choice enrollment grew from 287 in fall 2009/10 to 990 in fall 2015/16. Projections run from 12,470 (12,710 including the roughly 240 SCSE, ECP and GROW students) in 2016/17 to 12,524 (12,764 including) in 2020/21. A companion report covers the TSD Facilities Review Committee.

**Business items**
Bid #9817, roofing at 7 schools: J. D. Chandler $1,078,282.00 and Royal West $773,800.00, total $1,852,082.00, from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and Operational Fund. Bid #9818, lawn mowing and leaf removal: Green Meadows Lawnscape at $112,644 per year for three years from the General Fund. Bid #9819, Hamilton Elementary and International Academy-East upgrades: trade contracts totaling $2,909,738.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, the largest Contrast Mechanical at $1,632,700.00. Policy services: Lusk Albertson, not to exceed $15,000 plus $4,000 annually for updates, from the General Fund.

**Meeting and agenda.** Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, February 16, 2016, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, with video at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda runs recognitions; the General/Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum reports on Enrollment Projections and the Facilities Review Update; and Business items Bid Approval #9817, #9818 and #9819 plus the Policies Services Provider engagement.

**Recognitions.** Senior Scholar Athletes 2015-2016 honors athletes carrying a 3.5 grade point average at Troy High, Athens and the International Academy. Mr. Jolly reads the fall 2015 All-State list: Noah Arabbo (senior, Athens, boys soccer; coach Todd Heugh), Jennifer Cui and Naomi Kim (seniors, Troy High, girls golf; coach John Getzan), Michael Faber, Kevin Fietsam, Steve Forman (sophomore) and Sai Kagithala (junior) in boys tennis under coach Brian Miska, and Bogdan Pintilie (senior, Troy High, boys soccer; coach Jim Stachura). A resolution recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy. The TSD Mission Moment features Barnard fourth graders and teachers Debbie Rosenman and Nicole Coffer in the Oakland County Water Resources Commission Kids' Clean Water Calendar Contest, tied to the Michigan Studies unit on the Great Lakes watershed; from over 800 county entries Barnard produced four grand winners plus five other drawings in the 2016 calendar.

**January minutes.** The January 12, 2016 workshop, called to order by President Philippart at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building with Underwood absent, covered a Business Services update on the December cash position and budget report, M-Step results and county comparisons, and the 2016 NSBA Advocacy Conference; adjourned 7:45 p.m. The January 19, 2016 organizational and regular meeting opened at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building with Philippart, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Harris, Pass, West and Roncone, and approximately 40 members of the audience. Motions 16-001 through 16-015 all carried 7 yes to 0 no: Dr. Philippart elected President until December 31, 2016, Mr. Schmidt Vice President and Mrs. Fleming Secretary on the same term, and Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for January through December 2016, with Judy Holmes named temporary secretary and designated to post meeting notices. The fund depositories resolution names Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, First Merit Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank, authorizes Treasurer Rick West's facsimile signature with Superintendent Richard M. Machesky as emergency alternate, and permits investment under Board Policy D-1103 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code; certified by Paula Fleming on January 19, 2016. Legal counsel designated for 2016: Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk & Albertson; LaPointe & Associates, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. Further motions adopted the 2016 meeting calendar, approved the November 2015 Treasurer's Report and new hires Kyle von Plagenhoef and Jillian Sullivan, approved Mr. Pass as Director of Employee Services without tenure, approved the Beijing Weiming Education Group MOU for a pilot of ten Chinese students in their senior year, and approved Mr. Schmidt's attendance at the NSBA Advocacy Institute Conference in Washington, D.C., January 24-26, 2016. Troy High's "Caring for Karen" effort raised over $31,500 for the Karen Barrientos Cancer fund. Adjourned 8:53 p.m.

**Weiming update.** A January 22, 2016 email from Rich Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent (248-823-4011, rmachesky@troy.k12.mi.us), forwards word that Oakland Schools will not support Troy's work with Weiming under its SEVIS certification for F1 visas, because Weiming never submitted RFP documents for consideration as an Oakland Schools endorsed diploma-granting exchange. Troy would have to obtain its own SEVIS certification, a process described as arduous and taking more than 9 months, or partner with Educatius to keep hosting F-1 students through Oakland Schools; districts hosting Educatius students receive the per pupil allocation plus an additional $2000. Machesky states he is not comfortable allocating staff resources to certification at this time, which underlies consent item 5.D rescinding the Weiming resolution.

**Enrollment projections (item 7.A).** Mr. Dziatczak presents analysis dated February 2, 2016 by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., STANFRED Consultants. Headcount history: 12,182 in 2007/08, 12,069 in 2009/10, 12,328 in 2011/12, 12,573 in 2013/14, 12,556 in 2014/15 and 12,710 in 2015/16. Birth-to-kindergarten ratios climb from 4.42 in 98-99 to 6.18 in 13-14 and 5.82 in 14-15, with most-likely projections of 6.39 for 15-16 and 6.08 for 16-17; headcounts exclude 240 students in ECP, SCSE and GROW, and projections assume 100 Schools of Choice kindergartners and 50 in first grade. Schools of Choice enrollment: 287 in fall 2009/10, 416, 590, 700, 821, 907 and 990 in fall 2015/16. Projected enrollment excluding those 240 students runs 12,470 in 2016/17 (K-5 5399, 6-8 2955, 9-12 4116), 12,469 in 2017/18, 12,452 in 2018/19, 12,481 in 2019/20 and 12,524 in 2020/21, or 12,710, 12,709, 12,692, 12,721 and 12,764 including them. Future enrollment is calculated by adding the most likely plus the low projection divided by two. Item 7.B is a companion report by Mr. Dziatczak on the TSD Facilities Review Committee; both are reports requiring no action.

**Business items.** Bid Approval #9817, roof replacement and restoration at 7 schools, reviewed by district roofing consultant WeatherTech, Owner's Representative Michelle Kerns and Facilities Coordinator Katelyn Weaver: J. D. Chandler $1,078,282.00 and Royal West $773,800.00, total $1,852,082.00, as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and Operational Fund. Bid Approval #9818, district-wide lawn mowing and leaf removal, awarded to Green Meadows Lawnscape at $112,644 per year for the next three years from the 2015/2016, 2016/2017 and 2017/2018 General Fund. Bid Approval #9819, MEP upgrades at Hamilton Elementary and MEP upgrades with classroom construction at International Academy-East, reviewed by TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow: Professional Thermal demolition $44,687.00; Titan Industries general trades $185,951.00; Hewitt Company aluminum storefront $303,000.00; Steel Equipment Co. metal lockers $11,700.00; Farnell Contracting casework $32,700.00; Contrast Mechanical mechanical $1,632,700.00; and Great Lakes Power electrical $699,000.00; total $2,909,738.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

**Policies services provider (item 8.D).** The Board is asked to engage Lusk Albertson to review, prepare and maintain Board bylaws, policies and administrative regulations consistent with its proposal dated February 8, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $15,000 and $4,000 annually for updates, from the General Fund. The attached engagement letter of February 8, 2016, addressed to Mr. Rick West at 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098 and signed by Kevin T. Sutton of Lusk Albertson, PLC (direct dial 248-988-5695, KSutton@LuskAlbertson.com), records that Sutton met with the Board on February 2, 2016 and that standard administrative regulations are anticipated by the end of February 2016. All documents remain Lusk Albertson's copyrighted property under a continuing license to the District and carry a small legible ownership symbol. Costs: initial bylaws and policies $5,000.00 payable on delivery; initial administrative regulations $10,000.00 payable on delivery; annual updates to bylaws and policies $1,500.00 and to administrative regulations $2,500.00, billed on or about December 1st each year. The District may opt out with written notice at least 30 days before December 1st of any year.
